stories.headline: New York awards $45 million to expand forest markets and tree nurseries
stories.body: New York’s Department of Environmental Conservation announced US$45 million for 44 projects on October 29. The Advancing Forest Markets awards support native-tree supply, wood processing and markets for low-grade timber across the state.
stories.region: NEW YORK — ADVANCING FOREST MARKETS / OCTOBER 29 AWARDS

stories.headline: Acadian’s Maine harvesting improves as New Brunswick pulpwood demand weakens
stories.body: Acadian Timber’s third-quarter report shows diverging conditions across its New Brunswick and Maine timberlands. Companywide timber sales and services reached C$24.0 million, up from C$23.0 million a year earlier.
stories.region: CANADA / NORTHEAST — NEW BRUNSWICK AND MAINE / OCTOBER 28 RESULTS

stories.headline: Deschutes schedules Friday pile burning near La Pine

stories.headline: New forest monitor maps permanent conversion, with losses concentrated in the South
stories.body: A Clark University team’s October 29 report introduces the U.S. Forest Monitor, an open platform tracking permanent conversion of forests to development, cropland and other persistent nonforest uses.
stories.region: U.S. FORESTRY — LAND CONVERSION / OCTOBER 29 REPORT

featuredResource.title: Forest Carbon Online (FCO)
featuredResource.description: Forest Carbon Online is an independent web app for exploring and comparing state- and county-level forest-carbon estimates from USDA Forest Service inventory data. It presents sources and uncertainty information for broad-area comparisons, not parcel- or stand-level carbon accounting.
